articles.title: Finding Anchor in the Tsunami: Practical Wisdom and Spiritual Accountability in Times of Crisis
articles.description: Learn how Scripture and practical wisdom work together during times of crisis. Discover how Psalm 142 and the Passover story encourage faith, responsibility, and hope.
articles.summary: When life is shaken by crisis, fear can easily overwhelm us. This message combines biblical wisdom with practical responsibility, showing how faith in God and wise action help us remain steady during difficult seasons.
articles.author: Rev. Benson K Sunny

keyTakeaways.item: Keep a soft heart before God.

quiz.question: What did David do in his distress?
quiz.explanation: David honestly brought his fears before God.

quiz.question: What does the Passover story teach?
How should believers respond to fear?
quiz.explanation: Prayer anchors us in God's peace.

quiz.question: What spiritual danger does the sermon warn about?
quiz.explanation: A hardened heart resists God's correction.

articles.title: Overcoming Burnout and Panic: Finding Your Peace in a Chaotic World
articles.description: Struggling with stress and data-driven panic? Explore actionable steps from Psalm 23 to overcome anxiety and walk confidently through life's uncertain seasons.
articles.summary: When personal crises and confusing global shifts trigger overwhelming anxiety, it is easy to lose our way. Discover how shifting your focus to the Shepherd offers an unshakeable, practical peace that protects your mental and spiritual health.
articles.author: Rev. Benson K Sunny

keyTakeaways.item: Constantly analyzing the data and severity of a crisis will blind you to the spiritual vision and purpose God has set before you.
Human evaluations can only judge your current, visible circumstances and are completely incapable of predicting your future potential.
God frequently uses seasons of isolation and wilderness to shield you from harmful social pressures and quietly develop your character.
True spiritual peace is demonstrated when you take practical care of your health but leave the emotional weight of the outcome completely with the Shepherd.

quiz.question: What outward reason caused David's family to exclude him from the army and leave him in the wilderness?
options: He had repeatedly refused to pledge his loyalty to King Saul's royal guard.
He was required by local laws to stay behind as the sole caretaker of his mother.
He was explicitly trained in advanced musical instruments rather than physical warfare.
He was a cute child who lacked the muscular, manly build expected of a soldier.
quiz.explanation: The text points out that David did not look like a traditional, muscular warrior; because he looked like a cute kid, his family cornered him as the least capable of contributing to the army.

quiz.question: According to the sermon, what major advantage did David gain from being isolated in the wilderness during his childhood?
options: He was completely unaware of social pampering, which kept him from developing an inferiority complex.
He avoided catching the localized flus and plagues affecting the city.
He was able to amass a massive amount of personal wealth by trading wool.
He had ample time to study advanced military strategies from foreign books.
quiz.explanation: Because David was sent away early, he didn't realize or expect the passive pampering or validation of others, which turned out to be a hidden blessing that preserved his internal confidence.

quiz.question: What practical response does the speaker emphasize Christians must adopt besides prayer during an out-of-control crisis?
options: Moving to isolated rural areas to completely avoid contact with society.
Walking forward with a cool spirit, focusing on our duties while trusting God’s sovereign control.
Gathering global data to predict the exact date the trouble will end.
Launching a corporate business plan to protect personal finances from collapsing.
quiz.explanation: The sermon outlines that while prayer is necessary, we must also exercise active trust by keeping a cool spirit, fulfilling our duties, and refusing to let data-driven panic blur our vision.

quiz.question: Why does the speaker tell the audience to say 'no' to the evaluations of bosses, managers, or friends?
options: Because human evaluation can only see your current state and cannot see the hidden power God put inside you.
Because family members are always perfectly accurate in their predictions of your future.
Because church leaders are the only individuals legally authorized to evaluate your life.
Because seeking career promotions or workplace success is biblically discouraged.
quiz.explanation: Human beings evaluate based entirely on what is visible right now, meaning they are completely blind to the inner strength and future potential that God has prepared for your life.

articles.title: Why Am I So Stressed? How to Shift from Constant Worry to True Peace
articles.description: Burnt out by constant worry and trying to control the future? Learn how to step out of the stress cycle and rely on divine strength using timeless principles from 2 Chronicles.
articles.summary: When life hits a breaking point, it is easy to default to hyper-anxiety and fight-or-flight mode. Discover how the ancient strategy of Gideon reveals a practical blueprint to stop trying to fix everything yourself and let God carry the heavy lifting of your daily burdens.
articles.author: Rev. Benson K Sunny

keyTakeaways.item: We naturally experience anxiety when we treat life's challenges as battles we must win using our own strength and strategies.
God deliberately limits our resources and options so that we will stop relying on human pride and learn to trust His supreme power.
Committed journaling of your raw emotions and prayers creates an undeniable testimony of God's supernatural deliverance.
True spiritual rest is achieved when we show up responsibly but leave the ultimate results completely in God's hands.

quiz.question: According to 2 Chronicles 20:15, to whom does the battle ultimately belong?
options: The individual who works the hardest
The nation with the largest army
quiz.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:15 explicitly states, 'for the battle is not yours, but God's.'

quiz.question: Why did God insist on thinning out Gideon's army from 30,000 men?
options: The Midianite army was much smaller than originally anticipated.
There was a severe shortage of food and weapons for the soldiers.
He wanted to prevent Israel from pridefully boasting that they saved themselves.
Gideon requested a smaller, elite squad for a stealth attack.
quiz.explanation: God told Gideon that the people were too many, because Israel would claim glory for the victory and say they won by their own power.

quiz.question: What happened during Gideon's first test when he asked the fearful men to leave the battlefield?
options: Only a handful of soldiers decided to walk away.
All 30,000 men bravely chose to stay and fight.
The remaining army grew angry and revolted against his leadership
quiz.explanation: To Gideon's surprise, two-thirds of his total force (20,000 out of 30,000 men) admitted they were afraid and went home.

quiz.question: What practical tool does the sermon recommend to prevent us from rewriting our history with pride?
options: Memorizing complex theological definitions of human humility.
Avoiding any form of career promotion or personal achievement.
Asking church leaders to verify our daily career performance.
Recording an 'Emotion Equation' in a diary or phone before a crisis is solved.
quiz.explanation: Writing down your raw panic, lack of control, and prayers before a breakthrough prevents your pride from taking credit once the problem settles.

articles.title: Romans 8:1-11 — Life in the Spirit
articles.description: A Back to the Bible cell fellowship study on freedom in Christ and life by the Spirit, with reflection questions and a short quiz.
articles.author: ROLCC Fellowship Team

sections.heading: Observe
sections.body: Read Romans 8:1-11 slowly. Notice the contrasts Paul draws: condemnation vs no condemnation, flesh vs Spirit, death vs life and peace.

sections.heading: Interpret
sections.body: Paul teaches that those in Christ are set free from condemnation. The mind set on the Spirit brings life and peace.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Where do you feel condemnation or pressure this week? How might setting your mind on the Spirit change how you respond?

discussionQuestions: What does 'no condemnation' mean for believers in Christ?
How does Paul describe the difference between the flesh and the Spirit?
What is one practical way to 'set the mind on the Spirit' this week?

activities.title: Scripture meditation
activities.body: Rewrite Romans 8:1-2 in your own words and share one sentence with your group.

quiz.question: According to Romans 8:1, there is now no condemnation for those who are…
quiz.explanation: Paul grounds freedom from condemnation in union with Christ.

quiz.question: The mind set on the Spirit is life and…
quiz.explanation: Romans 8:6 contrasts death with life and peace.

quiz.question: Walking according to the Spirit means…
quiz.explanation: Paul calls believers to a Spirit-led way of life.

articles.title: Psalm 23 — The Lord Is My Shepherd
articles.description: A Back to the Bible study on God's care and guidance, with discussion questions for cell fellowship.
articles.author: ROLCC Fellowship Team

sections.heading: Observe
sections.body: Read Psalm 23 aloud. What images does David use to describe God's care?

sections.heading: Interpret
sections.body: David portrays God as a shepherd who provides, guides, protects, and restores.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: What valley are you walking through right now? How can you trust the Shepherd's presence?

discussionQuestions: Which phrase in Psalm 23 speaks most to you today?
How have you experienced God's provision or guidance recently?
